- **However, our records do not provide information** on whether the **required detailed inquiries into the cause of death** were conducted in these cases.

served_answer:
### Part 1: Legal Requirement
According to the law, when a person dies under suspicious circumstances, the police are required to conduct a thorough investigation into the cause of death. This is outlined in the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan)**, particularly in **Section 174**, which mandates that the police inquire and report on suicide, etc., and in **Section 176**, which provides for an inquiry by the magistrate into the cause of death. Additionally, **Punjab Police Rules-III**, **Rule 25.31**, specifies that an officer in charge of the police station must immediately send information to the nearest magistrate authorized to hold inquests and proceed to the place where the body is to hold an investigation in the manner prescribed by **Section 174** of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

### Part 2: Case Records
According to the summary of our own case records (Document 7), **10 of the 73 FIR(s)** that carry a recorded section cite **PPC §302** (which relates to murder). This indicates that **10 cases** involve deaths that are likely to be investigated under the provisions of **Section 174** and **Section 176** of the Code of Criminal Procedure. However, the summary does not provide specific details about whether the police conducted thorough investigations into the cause of death in these cases. It also does not mention whether the required reports, such as the plan of the scene of death, inventory of clothing, and other documents, were included in the police reports as required by **Punjab Police Rules-III**, **Rule 25.30** and **Rule 25.31**.

In conclusion, while the legal framework requires a thorough investigation into the cause of death in suspicious cases, the case records do not provide enough information to confirm whether these requirements were fully met in the 10 cases involving **PPC §302**.

served_answer:
### 1. Governing Provision and Its Substance:
The law requires that when a person dies under suspicious circumstances, the police must conduct a thorough investigation into the cause of death. This is outlined in **Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Pakistan)**, which mandates that the police inquire and report on suicide, unnatural death, or any other suspicious death. Furthermore, **Section 176** of the same code provides that in cases where a person dies while in police custody, or in other specified circumstances, the nearest magistrate empowered to hold inquests must conduct an inquiry into the cause of death. This includes recording evidence and following procedures to determine the cause of death accurately.

### 2. What Our Case Records Actually Show:
According to **our own case records (Document 7)**, out of **73 FIRs** that carry a recorded section cite, **10 FIRs** are linked to **PPC §302**, which pertains to murder. This indicates that in **10 cases**, the death was recorded as a result of murder, which is a form of suspicious death. However, the summary does not provide specific information on whether the police conducted detailed investigations into the cause of death in these cases or whether the required reports (such as those outlined in **Section 174** and **Rule 25.31**) were properly documented. It also does not specify whether the required elements (e.g., the plan of the scene of death, inventory of clothing, etc.) were included in the reports.

In conclusion, while the law clearly mandates that the police conduct thorough investigations into suspicious deaths, the case records do not provide enough detail to confirm whether these requirements were fully met in the cases where death was recorded as murder.

In conclusion, while the law clearly requires a thorough investigation and report in cases of unnatural or suspicious death, the case records do not provide enough information to determine whether the system has consistently followed these procedures in the cases involving death.

Rule 25.30

25.30.  Place of trial. - With regard to the place of trial of cases falling under Sections 179-183, Code of Criminal Procedure, police officers shall act solely with reference to the public convenience.

Ordinarily such cases shall be sent up for trial in the district in which the witnesses can attend with the least inconvenience to themselves.
